newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower on Rao woes.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower on Rao woes.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed sharply lower on foreign selling amid political uncertainty after the rejection of a bail plea by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a forgery case, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 9.74 points lower at 692.95.
"Prevailing political uncertainty in the country was main reason behind the ongoing slide in share prices," said Bharat Bhushan of brokers Nu-Era Equities.

A Delhi court dismissed a regular bail application by Rao and gave him until November 14 to appeal to a higher court. He was not arrested immediately, as he had an anticipatory bail allowed under Indian law to pre-empt possible arrest.
If denied bail by a higher court by November 14, Rao could be arrested and taken into custody.
Traders said the continued decline in ITC share prices was also a dampening factor.

ITC Ltd plunged 20.75 rupees, 7.17 percent, to 268.25 on massive selling by FIIs following arrests of two former chairmen on Friday by the Enforcement Directorate for alleged foreign exchange violations, brokers said.
Reliance Industries closed 2.80 rupees lower at 186.20 and TISCO lost 5.85 rupees to 166.75 on heavy selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs), they said.
State Bank of India fell 2.90 rupees to 216.35 and Larsen and Toubro eased 0.70 rupee to 216.80.
